name: Masterpiece Gallery
lore: The road wanders into a sunny riverside of famous old paintings, from a Sunday on La Grande Jatte to Van Gogh's bedroom, each one waiting to be dug out a block at a time.
sourceNote: Real public-domain paintings, CC0 open access from the Art Institute of Chicago, the National Gallery of Art, The Met and the Cleveland Museum of Art; licence re-read per object by lane C (game-research/sappers-path-v4/lands/06-masterpiece-gallery/README.md, picks-full.json: 50 picks, 12 spares, 3 held). Each file is a crop of the painting, never repainted (srcCrop on its manifest line, information only); converted by land.js boardOf with the whole manifest line (chroma). The folder keeps lane C's slug (06); as installed it is Land 4 in the factory's numbering (levels 351-400, era 12) and Zen World 5.

zen.note: v7 lane D: Masterpiece Gallery plays as Zen World 5 (tools/land.js ... zen writes tools/build-data/levels/zen.json only). Records keep the land factory numbers 351-400 (state.json from 351: Worlds 1-4 hold 1-50, 201-250, 251-300, 301-350); the page shows them on from World 4's last Zen number (main.js zenNum).

profile.note: Zen World 5, casual (v7 lane D, 2026-10-10): Dino Valley's profile as it ships (tools/lands/05-dino-valley/land.json): tags E18/N26/H6/X0 ending on a Hard, light deck features (? cards, linked squads), no locks, no archers, no Extreme, no mystery blocks (Peter, 2026-10-08), gentle moats (always 2 ways in) only on paintings that can carry one, careful floor 0.5 every tag. The 50 are lane C's real CC0 paintings (painting kind, shade on, manifest chroma where lane C set one).

hidden.note: v6 lane D8 (Peter, 2026-10-08): no mystery blocks in Zen, ever. The whole picture shows from the start; land.js and zen-world.js refuse a Zen land or world with hidden in its features or a hidden share.

deal.note: v7 lane D (trial bake, 2026-10-10): squads 1.6x the land default ([20, 50] at sizeRef 1400, scaled with the board as ever) and 400 deal attempts a candidate (96 before; a deal that lands early stops the loop, so only the hard boards pay). Lane C's paintings are max-box boards (up to 42 x 46, 1,890+ cells) whose colours lie in many scattered pieces: at the default size no deal met both the 55-tap cap and the 15 s longest tap on 25 of 50 boards (12 seeded attempts each, normal rules); at 1.6x on 4 of 50, and La Grande Jatte deals about 1 time in 200. The caps themselves are unchanged.

map.note: v7 lever 1: no new image bytes. The castle's sheets 2 (The Greenmarch: meadows, cottages, a river) and 5 (Fenwater Vale: a river garden) reused through map.fromLayout (their roads, level spots, side-quest spurs and bridges from map/layout.json and config map.bridges), alternately mirrored, under a warm painterly tint (map.tint on every entry) so they never read as the Campaign's own sheets.

eggNote: Eggs on the reused sheets' painted side-quest spur tips (World 1's rule; the land has no side quests, so no spur leads nowhere): eggTurns puts each sheet's 2 eggs on its template's 2 quest spots, each repeat its own pair. Kinds that suit a sunny riverside of meadows and gardens: grass, butterfly, mushrooms, reeds (the river garden sheet only).
credit: Public domain paintings from the Art Institute of Chicago, National Gallery of Art, The Met and Cleveland Museum of Art open access (CC0). Each level is a crop of the painting (never repainted) at the game's largest board; the full title, artist, date, museum, licence and the museum's own page are on its row.
